pending_commit.commit_message: bluetooth: Export GATT attribute interfaces as GATT client role In order to make the GATT attributes visible to D-Bus clients, this includes the following changes. - Adding gatt_interface_handler to export the discovered GATT services characteristics and descriptor to D-Bus - Implementation of observer mechanism in gatt.cc so that gatt_interface_handler can get notified on changes on GATT attributes - Determining how the D-Bus object properties should be updated and exported. We decided to go for the module where the interface handler needs to proactively go through all properties and update them. BUG=b:134425062 TEST=(1) Paired and connected to a BLE mouse from BT setting page. Verified in syslog that the D-Bus objects, methods and properties were exported for GATT services characteristics and descriptors. Ran subcommand "list-attributes" in bluetoothctl --service=org.chromium.Newblue and verified all attributes were printed. (2) Disconnected from the BLE mouse from BT setting page. Verified in syslog that the GATT attributes interfaces got removed and verified nothing got printed when running "list-attributes" subcommand with bluetoothctl --service=org.chromium.Newblue. Change-Id: If2b91c07531f12474aaa2ff9ac9f3e29d01fea44 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1716174 Tested-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu Liu <yudiliu@chromium.org>

bluetooth: Prevent exporting HID service via D-Bus and report completion of GATT browsing This uses a black list for hiding HID service from D-Bus clients for security reason until we come up with GATT profile manager. This also adds the logic to notify GATT observers on the completion of GATT browsing once all GATT attributes are resolved. However, if any error occurs during primary service enumeration or primary service traversal, GATT observer will not get notified on completion. BUG=b:138399390 TEST=(1) Pair and connect to a BLE mouse from bluetoothctl --service org.chromium.Newblue. (2) Invoke command "list-attributes" in bluetoothctl and verify that HID service and its attributes are not exported. (3) Disconnect from the mouse and observe that the all exported GATT attributes get unexported and "list-attributes" prints nothing. Change-Id: Ia7171a9379b0e17546da523b066db8b9a2eb9ef0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1726979 Tested-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu Liu <yudiliu@chromium.org>

bluetooth: Set ServicesResolved property to reflect freshness of GATT primary services This adds SetServiceResolved() in device_interface_handler so that when GATT has any update which effects the freshness of GATT attribute structures, GATT calls it to report the change, and device_interface_handler reflects the information on ServicesResolved property. This also fixes a bug where the updated flag of Property<T> variables of a device should be reset after exporting property update to D-Bus. BUG=b:134425062 TEST=(1) Connect to a BLE mouse via bluetoothctl and verify that ServicesResolved property becomes true. (2) Disconnect from the mouse via bluetoothctl and verify that ServicesResolved property becomes false. Change-Id: Ie15020e62571d784b3bb1dabba2885fdf67743d7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1730703 Tested-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu Liu <yudiliu@chromium.org>

mount-encrypted: add the new cmdline option "insecure" mount-encrypted doesn't store an insecure system key in NVRAM, which allows us to keep encstateful not wiped over TPM clearing and avoids potential unexpected behavior caused by soft-clearing TPM 2.0. The option should only be enabled for testing purposes and will be used in the autotest env. This CL provdes an alternative and simpler way to solve the soft-clearing TPM 2.0 problem mentioned above, compared with the original solution in CL:1753389. BUG=b:139399088 TEST=tested along with CL:1763468: On a chell, make sure the changes are no-op in any case. On a soraka, create the magic file in /mnt/stateful_partition, then 1. Run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and log in. Then, repeat those 3 steps a few times and make sure each time the encrypted partition is not wiped. Also, check if mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 2. Run tpm_softclear to soft-clear the TPM, then run tpm_manager_client take_ownership to re-own the TPM, then reboot. Make sure the encrypted partition isn't wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 3. Remove the magic file, run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and make sure the encrypted partition is wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it creates a random key and stores it in NVRAM. diagnostics: update cros_healthd's init script cros_healthd's ProbeNonRemovableBlockDevices method works outside of the minijail sandbox, but not inside. To fix this, we need to mount parts of /sys and /dev inside the minijail. cros_healthd attempts to discover nonremovable block devices programmatically, so it doesn't make sense to mount specific paths within /sys or /dev when these paths could vary per device or over time. Also, add the -G argument to the minijail call, so that cros_healthd enters the minijail as a member of the disk group. This is necessary to get access to the block /dev nodes. BUG=b:128683357 TEST=build and deploy diagnostics on nami. Add some test code to DeviceStatusCollector in Chrome which calls cros_healthd's ProbeNonRemovableBlockDevices Mojo method. Enterprise enroll the DUT, then check /var/log/chrome/chrome to make sure that Chrome was able to read information from cros_healthd.
